encoding.why: The sidecar loads on first paint on a phone, so the bulk payload is interned rather than pretty-printed. This block, plus schemaVersion, generatedOn, generatedBy, notes and derivationRules above it, are the parts meant to be read by a person.
encoding.topics: topics is [subjectSlug, [[unitSlug, [entry, ...]], ...]] in catalog order, then unit order, then topic order. A topic id is `topic:` + subjectSlug + `:` + unitSlug + `:` + entry[0]. A topic's ordinal is its position in that flattened walk, counting from 0.
encoding.entry: [slug, programs, estimatedStudyMinutes, sectionCharacterCount, exactQuestionCount, citationReviewQuestionCount, contentStatus, sourceIds, difficulty, relatedTopics]. The last two are optional and dropped from the right when absent; difficulty is -1 when it is absent but relatedTopics is present.
encoding.programs: An index into tables.programs, which holds each distinct programme array once.
encoding.contentStatus: An index into tables.contentStatus. That table lists every legal status, not only the emitted ones, so a code never changes meaning.
encoding.difficulty: An index into tables.difficulty, on the same all-legal-values basis as contentStatus.
encoding.sourceIds: Indices into tables.sources, in the entry's own order.
encoding.relatedTopics: Topic ordinals, in the entry's own order.
encoding.publish: Not stored. It is true exactly when contentStatus is source-grounded, so the reader derives it; see the publish rule in derivationRules.
encoding.layout: The header is pretty-printed, tables and topic subtrees are emitted one line per subject. Regenerate with `node scripts/build-topic-metadata.mjs`; `node scripts/validate-metadata.mjs` fails if the bytes on disk differ from a fresh derivation.

notes: prerequisites: omitted. There is no topic-to-topic ordering edge anywhere in the corpus, so any prerequisite chain would be invented.
examAlignment: omitted. No topic, question or catalog record names an exam blueprint, competency code or test plan section.

learningObjectives (as a structured array): omitted. sections.learningObjectives exists as free prose on the topic bundle and is served from there. Splitting it into discrete objectives would require rewriting source text, which the import contract forbids.
tags: omitted. Questions carry tags, but no tag vocabulary is attached to topics and propagating question tags upward would attribute claims to topics that their own source text does not make.

lastReviewed: omitted. The corpus records import and verification dates for source material, not a review of the published topic by a person. Reusing an import date as a review date would misrepresent it.
medically-reviewed as a contentStatus: never emitted. No content in this repository has a documented credentialed clinical review.
difficulty on topics below the evidence threshold: omitted rather than estimated. Most topics have no exact-mapped difficulty-bearing questions at all.
relatedTopics on topics with no co-mapped question: omitted rather than back-filled from titles, subjects or units.
license and author attribution: not held here at all. Source provenance lives in content-v2/indexes/source-registry.json and is referenced by sourceIds.
derivationRules: Scope: this file is a sidecar. It is joined to content-v2/subjects/ at runtime by topic id and never edits the corpus, so the mirror-equivalence and hard-coded totals asserted by validate-all-curricula.mjs stay intact.

programs: derived from the topic's subject category using a fixed mapping — pre-health-core -> pre-nursing, nursing, premed, healthcare; healthcare-foundations -> pre-nursing, nursing, healthcare; pathophysiology -> nursing, healthcare; allied-health -> healthcare. This is a category-level mapping, not a per-topic judgement about who should study the topic.

estimatedStudyMinutes: round(sectionCharacterCount / 900 + exactQuestionCount), clamped to [2, 90]. 900 characters per minute is a reading-rate assumption chosen for this build, and one minute is allowed per mapped question. It is a rough planning aid, not a measured or authoritative figure.
sectionCharacterCount: the summed length of every non-empty string in the topic's own sections object. sections.references is an array of citations rather than prose, so it is excluded.

exactQuestionCount: the number of questions whose mappedCanonicalTopicIds contains this topic id. This equals the topic bundle's availability.exactQuestions for all 1409 topics, which is asserted by validate-metadata.mjs.
citationReviewQuestionCount: of those same mapped questions, how many set citationReviewRequired === true.

difficulty: emitted only when at least 5 questions with mappingScope 'exact' map to the topic and carry a difficulty of foundational, intermediate or advanced. The modal value wins, ties broken in the order foundational, intermediate, advanced. foundational -> beginner, intermediate -> intermediate, advanced -> advanced. Questions with difficulty 'unknown' or with no difficulty field are excluded because they carry no signal. Difficulty is never guessed from a topic's title or subject.

contentStatus: derived from the topic bundle's own status — final -> source-grounded, final_requires_citation_review -> needs-medical-review, available -> draft. The value 'medically-reviewed' is never emitted: nothing in this repository evidences a credentialed clinical review, so claiming one would be a fabrication.

sourceIds: the `collection:<value>` id from the topic's own provenance.sourceCollection, plus a `reference-host:<hostname>` id for each distinct host in the topic's sections.references. Every id resolves to a record in content-v2/indexes/source-registry.json.

publish: true only for source-grounded topics. The brief's phrasing (publish when contentStatus !== 'draft') and its validator rule (never publish a needs-medical-review topic) disagree; the stricter, safer rule wins, so needs-medical-review topics are held back as well as drafts. It is not stored: it is a pure function of contentStatus, so the encoder asserts the rule holds for every topic and the reader re-derives it. A stored copy could only ever disagree with the status beside it.

relatedTopics: two topics are related when one question's mappedCanonicalTopicIds array lists both ids. Emitted as the up-to-6 most frequently co-mapped ids, sorted by co-occurrence count then id, excluding the topic itself. Omitted when the topic has no co-mappings. This is the only topic-to-topic edge evidenced anywhere in the corpus; there is no prerequisite graph.
generatedOn: copied from content-v2/catalog.json so regeneration is reproducible rather than wall-clock dependent.
Ordering: topics follow catalog order, then unit order, then topic order, and every list inside an entry is sorted deterministically, so the file regenerates byte-identically.

Encoding: the derived values above are the contract; the bytes on disk are an interning of them, described in this file's own `encoding` block. Repeated strings — source ids, programme combinations, the two enums, and the subject and unit halves of every topic id — are held once in `tables` and in the topic tree, and each entry cites them by integer. The header stays pretty-printed and the payload is emitted one line per subject. Interning is lossless and the reader in src/lib/content/metadata.ts reverses it, so every consumer still sees the full strings.
